title: Ruling 2022-05: Tax Applied to Transfer of a Lease Interest to Extend Lease
text:
Date: October 26, 2022

Written by: Emily Bergquist

Approved by: Craig Bolio, Commissioner of Taxes

This is a formal ruling for your client, [Taxpayer] regarding the applicability of property transfer tax to an assignment of lease and grant of options to renew. This ruling is based upon representations in your email dated [date].

Facts 

1. The [Church], (Church) as landlord, and [Initial Lessee] as tenant, entered into a ground lease dated June 10, 2010, for premises at [location], Vermont. The initial term of the ground lease is thirty years, beginning [date], and ending [date].

2. The ground lease provides the tenant one option to extend the lease term for ten years and a second option to extend the lease term for an additional 9 years and ten months. If both options were exercised the term of the ground lease would be 49 years and 10 months and would end on [date].

3. The ground lease does not contain an option for the tenant to purchase the leased premises.

4. By assignment dated [date], [Original Lessee] assigned its interest in the ground lease as tenant to [Assigned Lessee]. By assignment dated [date], [Assigned Lessee] assigned its interest in the ground lease to [Taxpayer].

You have asked the following questions:

Question 1: The remaining term of the ground lease, including the existing two options is approximately 37 years. If the ground lease were amended to provide the tenant with an additional option to extend the lease for a period of twelve years, which if exercised, would extend the lease to [date] October 31, 2071 (less than 50 years from now), would this amendment constitute a transfer of title to property under 32 V.S.A. Section 9601(3) requiring the payment of property transfer tax?

Question 2: If the ground lease were amended to provide tenant with options to extend the term of the ground lease beyond fifty years from the current date, would this amendment constitute a transfer of title to property under 32 V.S.A. Section 9601(3) requiring the payment of property transfer tax?

Question 3: If transfer tax is due under either of the above ground lease amendments, how would the transfer tax be calculated? Is it calculated on the gross rents due for the entire term of the ground lease, including extensions, without any present value discount or is it based on the fair market value of the leased premises?

Question 4: If the ground lease, following either of the amendments described above, was assigned by [Taxpayer] to a third party for consideration, would that assignment be subject to property transfer tax?

Discussion 

Property transfer tax is imposed on every transfer of title to property by deed or other writing. 32 V.S.A. § 9602. “Title to property” is defined as follows:

(3) "Title to property" includes:

(A) those interests in property that endure for a period of time the termination of which is not fixed or ascertained by a specific number of years, including an estate in fee simple, life estate, perpetual leasehold, and perpetual easement; and

(B) those interests in property enduring for a fixed period:

(i) equal to or exceeding 50 years;

(ii) less than 50 years if, by reason of a grant of right to extend the term by renewal or otherwise, said interest may be extended to a period equal to or exceeding 50 years;

(iii) less than 50 years if there is granted a right to purchase the property and there is granted the right to construct on the property a building or structure or to make such major capital improvements as water systems, sewer systems, roads, or parking facilities.

32 V.S.A. § 9601(3). A lease creates an “interest in property enduring for a fixed period.” If a lease is for a term or 50 years or longer, the transfer of that lease will be subject to transfer tax. If a lease is for a term of less than 50 years, but a right is granted to extend the lease term to a period equal to or exceeding 50 years from the date the right is granted, the grant of that right results in a transfer of an interest in property that will be subject to transfer tax.

An assignment of a lease is considered a “transfer” for purposes of the transfer tax:

(5) "Transfer" includes a grant, assignment, conveyance, will, trust, decree of court, transfer or acquisition of a direct or indirect controlling interest in any person with title to property, or any other means of transferring title to property or vesting title to property in any person.

32 V.S.A. § 9601(5).

In this case, [Church] granted an original lease to [Original Lessee] for a 30-year term, from [date] through [date], with no option to purchase. [Church] granted tenant [Original Lessee] an option to renew the lease for an additional 10 years, and granted [Original Lessee] an additional option to renew for another 9 years and 10 months, for a potential total lease term of 49 years and 10 months, ending [date]. [Church]’s transfer to [Original Lessee] was of an interest for a total of less than 50 years and therefore not subject to transfer tax. [Original Lessee] assigned that lease to [Assigned Lessee] in [year]. [Original Lessee]’s assignment to [Assigned Lessee] of the lease for a total of less than 50 years was also not subject to transfer tax.

[Assigned Lessee] then assigned the lease to [Taxpayer] in [year]. At that point, [Taxpayer] received a lease that ran from [year] through [year], a term of 23 years, plus option rights to extend the lease through [date], which would extend the lease to a potential term of 43 years, which is less than 50 years. [Assigned Lessee]’s assignment to [Taxpayer] was therefore also not subject to transfer tax.

Currently, [Taxpayer] holds a lease and rights to extend for a total of 37 years. If [Church] now grants [Taxpayer] an option to extend the lease for another 12 years, the term of the lease plus rights to extend would be 49 years (plus less than 2 months), through [date], a period of less than 50 years. The transfer of the new option would therefore not be subject to transfer tax.

If the new 12-year option to extend the lease is now granted to [Taxpayer] and [Taxpayer] then assigns the lease, the assignment would constitute a “transfer.” But since the term of the lease plus rights to extend to [year] would be less than 50 years, the assignment would not be subject to transfer tax.

If [Church] grants an option to extend the lease to a period that equals or exceeds fifty years from the date the option is granted, that grant would be subject to transfer tax.

Note that if there is any other written agreement that obligates [Church] to grant options to renew, that agreement would be considered part of the “transfer of title to property by deed or other writing.” The term of the promised options would be added to the lease-plus-current options to extend, and could result in a total potential lease term of 50 years or more, making the transfer taxable.

For purposes of the property transfer tax, the Department generally values leases using the total lease payments under the lease agreement including options to extend, adjusted to present value.

General Provisions 

Issuance of this ruling is conditioned upon the understanding that neither the taxpayer nor a related taxpayer is currently under audit or involved in an administrative appeal or litigation concerning the subject matters of the ruling. This ruling is issued solely to the taxpayer and is limited to the facts presented, as affected by current statutes and regulations.

Other taxpayers may refer to this ruling, when redacted to protect confidentiality, to see the Department's general approach, but the Department will not be bound by this ruling in the case of any other taxpayer or in the case of any change in the relevant statutes or regulations.

This ruling will be made public after deletion of the taxpayer’s name and any information which may identify the taxpayer. A copy of this ruling showing the proposed deletions is attached, and you may request within 30 days that the Commissioner delete any further information that might identify the taxpayer. The final discretion as to deletions rests with the Commissioner.

You have the right to appeal this ruling within 30 days. 3 V.S.A. §§ 808, 815.
